access_note: Dryad exposes the three named files publicly. No file was downloaded. These are measured root mineral concentrations from experimental fields, not crop yields, food-consumption records or a national nutrition survey.
description: Alamu, Maziya-Dixon and Dixon measured trace and macro elements in storage roots from 25 yellow-fleshed cassava genotypes and three white-fleshed checks. The plants grew at five experimental fields covering major Nigerian agroecological zones over two seasons. The named Dryad dataset contains one XLSX table about sampling effects, one CSV table about genotype and environment, and a short README under CC0. The provider describes iron, zinc, calcium, potassium and other measured elements from laboratory spectroscopy. A food-supply simulation could use these values to test how genotype and growing-location choices change the mineral content of cassava entering a regional food basket. Coverage is limited to the tested genotypes, fields and seasons. A limitation is that mineral content alone gives neither harvest yield nor nutrient intake, so the resource cannot estimate population nutrition without other data. No files were downloaded, leaving exact column coding and missing values unchecked. Related catalogue crop datasets describe yields and management; this deposit supplies measured nutrient composition.
name: Cassava root mineral composition across Nigerian genotypes and locations
